newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqi paper says several hurt in attack on Uday.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi paper says several hurt in attack on Uday.

text.p: An attempt on the life of Iraqi President Saddam Hussein's eldest son Uday, who was shot and wounded on Thursday, caused several casualties, an Iraqi newspaper indicated on Monday.
The government newspaper al-Jumhouriya said: "The attention and care paid by him (Saddam) to his son is the same that he gave to whoever was seriously wounded in the vicious crime."
It was the first admission by an Iraqi newspaper that there were other casualties in addition to Uday.
Jumhouriya said Saddam was seen visiting Ibn Sina hospital in Baghdad where Uday is being treated for wounds which according to official accounts are not serious.

Uday, 32, was shot on Thursday evening while driving through Baghdad's posh al-Mansour district. The spot has turned into something like a shrine, frequented by thousands of Iraqis slaughtering sheep and handing out sweets to celebrate his survival.
Festivities continued until midnight on Sunday, residents said.

Two opposition groups abroad have claimed responsibility for the attack but there has been no official confirmation of the identity of the gunmen. Iraqi authorities have said they were investigating the incident.
There has been no official comment on Uday's health since a terse statement by the presidential office on Thursday.
Baghdad state-run newspapers on Monday carried a speech by Saddam in which he said his two sons Uday and Qusay were no different from the sons of any other Iraqi.
The papers said Saddam made the remarks in response to congratulations from the Iraqi council of ministers, which he chairs, on the survival of his son.
"I have dealt with this vicious incident in the same way when hearing about the wounding of one of my comrades or one of commanding officers in the battles in defence of the homeland," Saddam said.
The official al-Qadissiya newspaper said several diplomats, officials and trade union leaders sent bouquets to Uday wishing him a speedy recovery.

Jumhouriya said Iraqis had seen "with their own eyes how the leader used to send his two dear sons, Uday and Qusay, to take part in the great battles during the glorious Qadissiyat Saddam (1980-1988 Iraq-Iraq war) and the eternal Mother of Battles (1991 Gulf War)..."
Shebab (Youth) television said on Friday that Saddam's son personally contacted Iraq's soccer team in Dubai where they were competing in the quarter-finals of the Asian Cup games.
Uday owns the channel as well as Iraq's most influential newspaper Babel.
